tactics.name: Balanced 4-1-2-1-2 Diamond
tactics.description: A compact narrow 4-1-2-1-2 built around central combinations, two strikers and full-backs supplying most of the width.
tactics.whyGood: It creates central numerical superiority and strong links between DM, midfield, AMC and two forwards.

tactics.name: Balanced 4-4-2
tactics.description: A simple two-banks-of-four structure with natural width and two complementary forwards.
tactics.whyGood: It is easy to recruit for, tactically clear and gives a useful baseline against more specialised systems.

tactics.name: Positive 4-2-3-1 Wide
tactics.description: A proactive 4-2-3-1 using a double pivot behind three attacking midfielders and one striker.
tactics.whyGood: The pivot stabilises build-up while the front four occupy several attacking lines.

tactics.name: Positive 4-3-3 DM Wide
tactics.description: A modern 4-3-3 with a holder, two eights and complementary wide forwards.
tactics.whyGood: It offers strong pitch coverage, good rest defence and multiple progression routes.

tactics.name: Counter 3-5-2 Wing-Back
tactics.description: A back-three counter system using wing-backs for width and two forwards as immediate outlets.
tactics.whyGood: Three centre-backs protect the box while two forwards keep counter-attacking threat high.

tactics.name: High-Press 4-3-3
tactics.description: An aggressive 4-3-3 designed to regain possession high and sustain pressure in the opposition half.
tactics.whyGood: The front three, energetic midfield and compressed defensive line make it easier to surround the ball.

tactics.name: Balanced 4-1-4-1
tactics.description: A compact 4-1-4-1 with a dedicated screen behind a four-man midfield.
tactics.whyGood: It gives strong defensive spacing and central control while retaining wide outlets.

tactics.name: Defensive 5-3-2
tactics.description: A deep five-defender system prioritising central protection and counter-attacking through two forwards.
tactics.whyGood: It packs the box while still keeping two outlets available after regains.

tactics.name: Defensive 4-5-1
tactics.description: A conservative five-man midfield shape designed to deny central space and protect a result.
tactics.whyGood: The dense midfield makes progression difficult and keeps defensive responsibilities simple.
keyRequirements: Lone striker able to compete alone

tactics.name: Attacking 4-3-3
tactics.description: An aggressive 4-3-3 committing full-backs, midfield runners and wide forwards to attack.
tactics.whyGood: It creates several simultaneous attacking lanes and is useful when the team must force the game.

tactics.name: Attacking 3-4-3 Wing-Back
tactics.description: A front-foot back-three system with wing-backs stretching the pitch and a front three occupying the back line.
tactics.whyGood: Three defenders permit aggressive wing-back positions and five-lane attacking occupation.

tactics.name: Low-Block 4-4-2
tactics.description: Two compact banks of four with two forwards retained as direct counter outlets.
tactics.whyGood: It keeps defensive jobs simple while preserving an immediate route out after regains.

tactics.name: Control Possession 4-2-3-1
tactics.description: A patient 4-2-3-1 that controls territory and circulates until space opens between or outside the opposition lines.
tactics.whyGood: The double pivot gives secure circulation while the AP and wide attackers provide several receiving lines ahead of the ball.

tactics.name: Vertical Tiki-Taka 4-3-3 DM
tactics.description: Short combinations are used to progress quickly rather than simply retain possession, with runners attacking spaces created by circulation.
tactics.whyGood: The playmaking DM anchors build-up while the eights and front three provide vertical movement and penetration.

tactics.name: Gegenpress 4-2-3-1
tactics.description: An intense 4-2-3-1 intended to regain the ball immediately after losing it and attack before the opponent reorganises.
tactics.whyGood: Four aggressive attackers lead the press while the pivot balances ball winning and distribution behind them.

tactics.name: Direct Counter 4-4-2
tactics.description: A compact 4-4-2 that accepts periods without the ball and attacks space quickly after regaining possession.
tactics.whyGood: The DLF provides an outlet while the AF and wide runners attack the space left by an advanced opponent.

tactics.name: Route One 4-4-2
tactics.description: A deliberately direct system that moves the ball forward early toward a physical target and runners attacking second balls.
tactics.whyGood: The Target Man gives long passes a destination while the AF, wide players and midfield compete for territory and knockdowns.

tactics.name: Wing Play 4-4-2
tactics.description: A width-first 4-4-2 designed to stretch the opponent and generate repeated crossing opportunities for two forwards.
tactics.whyGood: Wide midfielders and overlapping full-backs create outside overloads, with a Target Man giving crosses a clear focal point.

tactics.name: Fluid Counter 4-1-4-1
tactics.description: A compact 4-1-4-1 that counters through short combinations and supporting runs rather than immediately launching long balls.
tactics.whyGood: The DM stabilises the block while the Box-to-Box midfielder and wide players quickly join the AF after regains.

tactics.name: Possession 4-1-4-1
tactics.description: A lower-risk possession structure with a playmaker at the base and four midfielders offering short passing options ahead.
tactics.whyGood: The DM acts as a circulation hub and the compact midfield keeps support distances short.

tactics.name: Positive 4-3-1-2 Narrow
tactics.description: A narrow 4-3-1-2 using three central midfielders and an advanced playmaker behind two complementary forwards.
tactics.whyGood: It overloads central zones while the wing-backs provide the width that the midfield shape lacks.

tactics.name: Balanced 4-4-1-1
tactics.description: A conventional 4-4-2 defensive shell with one attacker dropping into the number-ten line to connect midfield and the lone striker.
tactics.whyGood: The AMC reduces striker isolation while preserving two clear banks of four without the ball.

tactics.name: Counter 3-4-1-2
tactics.description: A cautious back-three system retaining an AMC and two strikers so regains can become attacks without waiting for many players to advance.
tactics.whyGood: The AMC, DLF and AF form an immediate counter-attacking triangle while the back three protect against turnovers.

tactics.name: Positive 3-4-2-1
tactics.description: A modern back-three system using two central attacking midfielders to occupy the half-spaces behind a single striker.
tactics.whyGood: Two number tens work between the lines while wing-backs hold width, creating five distinct attacking lanes.

tactics.name: Attacking 4-2-4
tactics.description: A high-risk structure that immediately puts four players against the opposition back line and is intended to force the game.
tactics.whyGood: The DLF supplies some connection while the other three attackers threaten depth and width around the box.
keyRequirements: Two midfielders able to cover huge spaces

tacticResearchNotes.purpose: Broad baseline template set for squad-fit and tactical comparison; not claimed to be a set of optimal FM20 meta tactics.
design: Templates cover genuinely different structures/styles rather than many near-duplicates.
Every added tactic uses only role keys already present in the supplied catalogue.
Descriptions and requirements are intended to support later tactical-coherence scoring and UI explanation.
Long-term design should allow role/duty optimisation within formations instead of treating templates as immutable.
